what_happened: Research found that the exact write-side collapse mechanism this task needs (tags.occurrence via --tags-json) was already fully designed and documented in issue-log.md's Occurrence Collapse section, with scope-excursion named explicitly as its intended first use case, but had zero real callers anywhere in the codebase. No new schema or CLI change to issue-record.sh or orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh is needed at all -- the fix is purely emitter-side at the two confirmed call sites, reusing an existing seam rather than inventing one.

context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's 'Three Containment sites, not one' section asserts 'the warning and the issue row every site already fires on a drop' across all three Containment sites, but orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (h)/(i) EXCURSION DROPPED filter (Site 1) only ever echoes a stderr warning and never calls issue-record.sh -- confirmed by grep for both 'EXCURSION DROPPED' occurrences, neither adjacent to an issue-record.sh call. This looks like doc/code drift rather than a deliberate asymmetry; left as an explicit plan-time decision point per the dispatch's instruction to confirm before changing.

The dispatch description's mechanism citations (git-commit-phase.sh 'around line 286', git-commit-scoped.sh 'around line 655') are stale: the live --class "scope excursion" emission sites are at lines 779 and 888 respectively, matching the research report rather than the description. The description itself instructed re-derivation, so the cost was one grep; the structural claim the citations carried (one issue-record.sh call per dropped path, from inside a per-path loop, at exactly two sites) is confirmed intact at the new line numbers.

validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification measurement extracts every test-*.sh token anywhere in the justification block as a claimed suite name, so writing the covering check in its fully-qualified form (verify-touched.sh followed by the phase's declared paths, which include a tests/test-*.sh file) is scored as a fabricated coverage claim for a suite the selector does not return. It also requires the claim to name the selector's ENTIRE output, not a representative subset. Both were corrected by naming the command without path arguments and enumerating the full returned suite list per phase; one phase whose touched set includes the deploy manifest was moved to the full tier with a cross-cutting-surface justification instead, since its selector output runs to roughly three dozen suites.

The research report's recommendation set was directly plannable with no re-derivation beyond confirming line numbers and one selector run per phase: it had already settled representation, collapse site, and the read-side no-change finding, and had pre-identified the shared-library precedent the two emitters already follow. Planning cost was correspondingly low.
